findings.summary: R1 milestone mapping includes M2 (Work Plan Compilation) but requirement text does not explicitly mandate work plan stage validation of plan_package_final.json acceptance; M2 should validate no semantic drift but R1 is about input acceptance which is purely M1 scope.

evidence.note: R1 text focuses on input acceptance and rejection of non-canonical sources
M1 exit criteria cover input validation and acceptance
M2 validates no semantic deviation but this is scope control not input acceptance
evidence.quote: No semantic deviation from frozen plan entities; validator confirms no new R#/AT#/O#/K# introduced (K1 mitigation).

findings.summary: R2 and R3 both map to M1 and M2 milestones, but the requirement text states these schemas are required 'before any code-generation stage begins' (R2) and 'before any workspace-writing stage begins' (R3). M2 (Work Plan Compilation) does not perform code generation or workspace writing per its deliverables, so M2 mapping appears conservative but not strictly required by the requirement text.

evidence.note: R2 requires repo_context.json before code-generation stage
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any code-generation stage begins

evidence.note: R3 requires workspace_context.json before workspace-writing stage
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any workspace-writing stage begins

evidence.note: M2 produces work_plan.json but does not generate code or write workspace canonical artifacts per stage restrictions

However, the sample check does not verify that M1 exit criteria explicitly test rejection of chat logs and non-canonical artifacts as specified in AT1 procedure, only that plan_package_final.json is accepted.
